title: multi-ticket build with four agents on disjoint work (#1366)
spec: SPEC.md section 3, scenario S1; fixture F1 tallykit

arm_notes.K3: K3 is not run at M0 (SPEC section 2.2); it joins when the arms review (#1365) has accepted its text

roles.note: Role members of the arms K3 and B1-roles (#1421, SPEC section 2.2): each is its own agent process with its own cap (per_role_usd, a tenth of the run cap: the integrator and the supervisor mostly wait), the roles model (null: the agent model; --roles-model overrides) and its own line in the run record (roles.members, spend.roles_usd). grace_s is how long they may run on after every worker has ended; max_restarts is how many replacements the supervisor may start for one worker. Both arms stay out of the M0 set until the human approves them and their budget (SPEC section 12).

n_per_arm.note: SPEC section 6.1: 10 per arm at M0 (the human approves, section 12), 3 for the quick subset after an epic, labelled exploratory

caps.basis: SPEC section 8.1: S1 assumed at 2.00 USD a run on Haiku, so 3x per run (6.00) and 1.25x the 80 USD estimate for 4 arms x 10 runs (100). Proposals; the human changes them before M0 (#1380).

metrics.primary_note: #1522, metric_version 2: the primary is the integration outcome, the thing four agents can only get right by coordinating on the two shared files and main. units_completed (the 8 modules, each with one owner) measures what each agent can implement alone: the pilot (#1365) had every arm fail the tokenizer unit on Haiku (the contract makes `12.` the tokens `12` and `.`, no visible test covers it), so that unit is a model-ability constant and units_completed is reported as a secondary, never as the headline. report.py counts a run as complete when integration_ok is true.

definitions.integration_ok: True when, on the final main, the four structural checks all pass: `registry` (tallykit/__init__.py imports every module exactly once and exports every function as a callable: the check imports the package, so it also fails when a module cannot be imported), `changelog` (exactly the four expected ticket lines), `no-conflict-markers` (no conflict marker in a tracked file) and `visible-tests` (the repository's own tests pass). False when any fails; null when the checker did not report one of them. Computed by the harness from outcome_checks (scenario.integration_ok), kept in metrics.integration_ok and scenario_metrics.integration_ok. No module's hidden behaviour test is part of it. Limit: the checker's marker scan covers every tracked file including the B1 board TASKS.md, where a conflict marker left in the board fails it (#1461 I1); the checker owner decides whether the board is excluded.
definitions.units_completed: Secondary (model ability). Modules that pass the hidden property tests on the final main (0 to 8; two per ticket, so a ticket is complete when both of its modules count). From the checker's unit checks, which are the 8 modules.
definitions.duplicate_work: Units (modules) whose path was changed by a non-merge commit of more than one agent, counted from git authorship (each agent commits under its own name) over the origin and every agent's clone. The setup commit is excluded. A module touched by an agent that does not own it is also listed in scenario_metrics.foreign_edits.
definitions.overwrites: Registry or changelog lines (lines matching the entry pattern of a shared file) that were added by some non-merge commit in the origin or any clone and are absent from the final main: lost lines. A line removed and added again counts as present. Lines lost before ever being committed are invisible here; the final registry and changelog checks catch those.
definitions.git_conflicts: Bash results of an agent that show a merge conflict (from the stream, as for every scenario); separate from overwrites and never summed with them.
definitions.merge_state: From the checker: clean, conflicts-left (conflict markers in a tracked file) or tests-broken (the visible tests fail on main).

store_metrics.source: artifacts.store_export, the counts-only report of the K arms' run store (klatch-bench store-stats, #1433), the same report as klatch admin stats --json; the metrics below are in scenario_metrics.store
store_metrics.arms: K1, K2, K3. B0 and B1 have no klatch store: null, with scenario_metrics.store.reason saying so

fields.claim_conflicts: claims.history.conflicts_handled: a claim refused and later granted to the same member (also metrics.claim_conflicts)
fields.claims_refused_by_rule: claims.history.refused, summed (every refusal carries a rule word)
fields.time_to_first_answer_s: asks.first_answer_median_secs, null when no ask was answered by someone other than the asker
fields.asks_cross_check: asks created and answered from the streams (asks.py) next to the store's counts, with match and differences; a mismatch is flagged in the record's notes and is never resolved silently
